panels.figure_caption: (A) Initial fundus photographs, FAG, and SD-OCT of a 34-year-old male who presented with suddenly decreased vision for 2 days in the right eye. The whitish lesions we observed in the patient were interesting. The whitish plaques were in the superficial retina (Figs. 3 and 4) mimicking cotton wool spot. However, OCT depicted well demarcated oval shaped lesion in the RNF layer with posterior shadowing. The size of these plaques was about 100 to 150 μm in diameter, and larger than toxocara larvae or eggs.
